readerTitle: Your restaurant is full. Should you open a second one?
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션 (만두 식당의 2호점 결정) · 모든 인물과 수치는 설명용
insight: 2호점은 1호점의 복사본이 아니다. 1호점이 왜 잘되는지 뜯어보고, 현장을 직접 보고, 다음에 일어날 일과 여유 자금까지 따져야 같은 성공을 옮길 수 있다.
misconception: 1호점이 잘되면 같은 메뉴와 인테리어를 그대로 옮기기만 해도 2호점도 잘된다.

sources.text: THK-01 유닛의 사고 모형 (제1원리, 지도와 영토, 2차 사고, 안전 마진)
모든 인물, 장소, 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 모든 수치는 설명용 가상 수치입니다. 자금 계산: 저축 $150,000 − 인테리어 $90,000 = 여유 자금 $60,000. 월 손실 $10,000 기준 6개월분입니다. $120,000을 쓰면 여유 자금은 $30,000, 즉 3개월분입니다.
6개월 뒤 결과: 1~5개월 손실 $10,000 × 5 = $50,000, 6개월째 손익분기. $60,000 − $50,000 = $10,000이 남습니다. $30,000만 남겼다면 3개월째 말에 자금이 바닥납니다.
하루 12,000명 유동인구 수치는 가상 중개 보고서의 숫자입니다. 실제 통계로 읽히지 않도록 카드에 'broker's report'로 표시했습니다.

cards.title: Your restaurant is full. Should you open a second one?
body: Dana runs a 40-seat dumpling restaurant. For three years there has been a line at lunch most days. Then a landlord across town offers her a space.
Over the next four cards, you make Dana's calls. Each one uses a different way of thinking from this unit.

image.label: A busy dumpling restaurant with a line outside
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 작은 만두 식당 앞에 점심 줄이 서 있고, 오른쪽 위에 말풍선처럼 '빈 점포' 간판이 걸린 다른 가게가 작게 보임. 실제 상호나 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Before looking at the new space, what do you write down?

options.text: What customers praise in reviews: the menu, the decor, the friendly vibe
options.feedback: Useful, but reviews show what customers notice, not what makes the numbers work. Some causes of success are invisible to them.

options.text: Each reason the first restaurant makes money, broken down piece by piece
options.feedback: You list them: the recipes, two skilled cooks, nearby office workers, rent below market, and you on the floor every night. Two of those won't move across town: the cheap rent and you.

options.text: This year's revenue and profit, then plan to double them
options.feedback: Fast, but it assumes everything behind those numbers comes along. You'd learn which parts don't the hard way.

choice.afterReveal: Break success into its basic parts before you copy it. Not every part travels.

cards.title: The broker says 12,000 people pass by every day.
body: Say you chose B. The broker's report shows more foot traffic than your current street. The landlord wants an answer this week.

options.text: Sign. The numbers beat your current spot
options.feedback: The report counts people walking past, not people who would stop to eat. You could commit to years of rent based on the wrong count.

options.text: Ask the broker for more data first
options.feedback: More detail helps, but it's still someone else's summary. The report can't tell you why people are on that street.

options.text: Sit across the street at lunch, dinner and on a weekend, and watch
options.feedback: You see busy lunches from nearby offices. But most evening traffic is commuters rushing to the train. You plan a lunch-focused shop with shorter evening hours.

cards.softwareNote: A market-size report is a map too. Ten calls with possible customers in the new market show you things the report can't.

cards.title: Who runs the new kitchen?
body: Say you chose C. You sign a lease for a lunch-focused shop. Ken, your best cook, is excited to lead the new kitchen.

options.text: Send Ken. The new shop needs your best person
options.feedback: The new shop gets off to a strong start. Then dumplings at the first shop slip, and regulars notice. You've weakened what pays the bills.

options.text: Move there yourself and leave your manager in charge of the first shop
options.feedback: You protect the launch, but you're the piece you found wouldn't travel. The first shop loses its nightly owner all at once.

options.text: Hire a cook now, have Ken train them for two months, then let Ken lead the new kitchen
options.feedback: The opening comes later and costs two months of extra wages. But when Ken leaves, the first shop keeps its quality.

cards.title: How much of your savings do you spend?
body: Say you chose C. You have $150,000 saved. The fit-out you like costs $120,000. Your plan says the new shop will lose about $10,000 a month until it breaks even in month four.

options.text: Spend all $150,000 on a fit-out that really impresses
options.feedback: A beautiful room, but the first slow month has to be paid from the first shop's cash. One surprise could put both shops at risk.

options.text: Spend $120,000 and keep $30,000, exactly enough for three months of losses
options.feedback: It feels careful, but it only works if the plan is right. Your plan needs four months, and plans tend to run late.

options.text: Trim the fit-out to $90,000 and keep $60,000, enough for six months
options.feedback: The room is plainer. In return, you can survive the plan being off by 50%.

cards.title: The plan was wrong. The buffer wasn't.
body: The new shop broke even in month six, not month four. Five months of losses cost **$50,000**.
With $30,000 in reserve, Dana would have run out of cash in month three, just as lunch regulars were starting to come back. With $60,000, she still has $10,000 left.
None of Dana's choices made the new shop succeed. They kept it alive long enough to find out.

image.label: Two cash jars draining over six months
image.brief: 두 개의 유리병에 동전이 들어 있음. 왼쪽 '$30,000' 병은 3개월째에 비고, 오른쪽 '$60,000' 병은 6개월째에도 바닥에 조금 남아 있음. 아래에 1~6개월 눈금.

cards.title: Careful thinking has a price.
body: Every best choice here cost something: weeks of watching the street, two months of extra wages, a plainer room. Another tenant might have taken the space while Dana was still watching.

These habits don't promise a hit. They cut out the avoidable mistakes. A second location is also a different job: running managers, not a kitchen. Some owners find that job sits outside what they do best.

cards.title: Copy the reasons, not the restaurant.
body: Each decision used one idea from this unit:
list: **Decision 1 · First principles:** break success into the parts that cause it
**Decision 2 · The map is not the territory:** the report isn't the street
**Decision 3 · Second-order thinking:** ask what happens to the first shop next
**Decision 4 · Margin of safety:** leave room for the plan to be wrong
cards.callout: **Try it today:** write down three reasons your business works. Next to each one, note whether it would survive a move to a new place.
cards.softwareNote: Launching in a second country or for a second customer type works the same way. If founder-led sales won the first market, ask who sells in the second, and how many months of runway you have if it takes twice as long.
